paras: The beating of Pearl at the Avondale picnic was a crowd attack on a Black man at a picnic of Baltimore and Ohio railroad employees at Avondale, on the Licking Reservoir in Ohio, on Saturday, August 29, 1885. According to the only report found, Pearl had struck a white man and was then "assaulted by the crowd and terribly beaten."

The attack took place during a picnic held by the "B. & O. employes" at Avondale, on the Licking Reservoir. The report gives no account of how many people attended, of the white man involved, or of what led to the blow.

Pearl, described only as "a colored man named Pearl," was said to have struck a white man at the picnic. The crowd then assaulted him and, in the report's words, he was "terribly beaten." The nature of his injuries and whether anyone intervened are not stated.
No report of arrests, of charges against Pearl or his attackers, or of Pearl's condition after the beating was found in the coverage.

The episode appeared as a single sentence in the "Condensed Telegrams" column of the Wheeling Register on Monday, August 31, 1885, between items on a family reunion, a postmaster's suicide and a horse-race offer. The item put the blow Pearl was said to have struck first, as the apparent cause, and named neither the white man nor anyone in the crowd. No local Ohio account, follow-up or Black-press report of the attack was found.
